title: Introduce token runway prognostics and probabilistic SLO forecasting dashboard
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Production customers increasingly ask not just for current token/latency cost telemetry but for short-term forecasts that help platform and customer teams answer: how long will a given token budget or latency SLO hold at current load and growth trends? This PR adds a lightweight prognostics pipeline and an interactive dashboard that surfaces per-tenant and per-route 'token runway' estimates and probabilistic SLO breach forecasts.

Scope and changes: single continuous set of changes across instrumentation, ingestion, forecasting, dashboard, and alert tuning: 1) metric instrumentation: new rolling-window metrics (runway_tokens_remaining, runway_rate_trend, latency_slo_tail_prob) exported from the gateway and runtime with tenant+route labels; OTEL spans enriched with forecast_anchor tags so traces can be correlated with forecasts. 2) forecasting worker: a small streaming estimator (exponential smoothing + short-window AR) that computes 5/15/60-minute horizon percentiles for token consumption and latency tail probability per tenant/route; published as Prometheus-style metrics and a compact protobuf payload to the observability ingestion topic. 3) dashboard: Grafana panels (JSON) that show runway horizon, forecast bands, probability heatmap of SLO breach, and an interactive selector for tenants/route groups. 4) alert tuning: new alert rules that switch to probabilistic mode—alert fires only when 95th percentile breach probability exceeds threshold for two consecutive windows; provides auto-suppression for noisy short bursts. 5) runbook + rollout: runbook for on-call and migration steps, and a controlled rollout via feature-flag gated by tenant tier.

Implementation notes: forecasting worker is implemented as services/observability/runway/estimator with a bounded in-memory state keyed by tenant_id+route_hash and a fallback path that uses simple linear extrapolation if windows are sparse. Forecast payloads are intentionally compact (utf8 proto) and published to the existing observability topic (obs.forecasts.v1). We reuse existing ingestion parsers and added a scheduled consumer to hydrate timeseries for Grafana streaming panels. To keep runtime overhead low, token-level counters are emitted at 15s intervals and aggregated to 1m for forecasting.

Backward compatibility & data retention: metrics have additive names (runway_*) and do not change existing metrics. Forecast payloads are optional: dashboards fall back to raw time series if forecasts are missing. We included an integration test mode that runs the estimator against historical traces for accuracy regression checks.

Rollout plan: 1) deploy forecasting worker to staging with feature flag off for all tenants; 2) enable for internal tenants and validate dashboard and runbook playbook for 48h; 3) enable on a small set of tier-2 customers for 72h while monitoring false positive rate; 4) gradual ramp to all customers over two weeks with opt-out.

Risk and mitigation: false positives from over-sensitive thresholds are mitigated by requiring two consecutive windows and a minimum traffic floor before alerts are eligible. Forecasting worker is stateless enough to be restarted without data loss. We added metrics for estimator health: forecast_lag_seconds, model_fail_rate, and fallback_rate.

Testing performed: unit tests for estimator logic (exponential smoothing math, input sanitization), e2e test that replays a recorded week of traffic to validate runway estimates vs ground truth, integration tests for dashboard ingestion and alert rule evaluation, and CI checks for linter and proto compatibility.

Related work: builds on ENG-1683 (per-tenant token budget counters) and ENG-2011 (dashboard streaming panels). Linear/PM refs: ENG-2145, PM-1987.

Checklist: - [x] instrument metrics and spans - [x] implement streaming estimator - [x] dashboard panels added - [x] alert rules and runbook - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] staged rollout plan documented

Notes: this PR is observability-only, no changes to public API or hosted inference runtime behavior beyond low-overhead metrics emission.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice end-to-end. Two questions: 1) how stable are the forecasts under diurnal traffic? 2) can we avoid adding more high-cardinality metrics?

Maya Chen: Reply: Forecast uses short-window seasonality-aware smoothing plus a traffic-floor check; we only emit runway_* metrics for tenants with traffic over the floor and aggregate route->route_group in high-cardinality cases.
Leila García: Suggestion: include a 'confidence' sparklines panel next to the runway so oncall can eyeball model certainty quickly.
Maya Chen: Added confidence band panel in runway-dashboard.json and implemented model_confidence metric exposed by the estimator.
Samir O'Neill: CI flaked on proto-compat; re-run fixed it. Approving with a follow-up to add an adaptive smoothing hyperparameter for specific tenants.
Leila García: Approved after verifying the runbook steps in staging.
Arjun Patel: Merging — please follow the rollout plan strictly and ping SRE during tenant ramp.
Maya Chen: Will do; feature flag gating and rollback plan included in runbook.
release_notes: Add token runway prognostics and probabilistic SLO forecasting: new runway_* metrics, forecasting worker, Grafana dashboard, probabilistic alert rules, and runbook. Provides short-horizon (5/15/60m) forecasts and SLO breach probabilities to reduce noisy alerts and enable proactive capacity planning.
project_impact: Observability visibility and alert behavior; low runtime overhead; opt-in via feature flag for tenant groups.
testing_summary: Unit tests for forecasting math, e2e replay test against one-week traffic, integration tests for ingestion and dashboard; CI passes; staging run validated for internal tenants.
